headline: All three EPSO reasoning tests are now live in CS/SK/EN: verbal reasoning (20 statements, 35 minutes) is built on verbatim EUR-Lex passages, and every key held under blind checks in all three languages. The last 20 unverified governance/policy questions are settled: 8 verified (6 after correction) and 12 marked unverifiable, so 139 of 151 are now verified.

shipped.title: Verbal reasoning in Czech, Slovak or English: 20 statements, 35 minutes
Verify the last 20 governance/policy questions: 8 verified (6 after correction), 12 marked unverifiable

verbal.format_source: Notice of Competition EPSO/AD/430/26, OJ C/2026/4668, section 4.3.2(b), Table 3, read from the Publications Office (Cellar) on 2026-10-29: verbal reasoning, language 1, 20 questions, 35 minutes, pass 10/20.
verbal.passages: 14 recitals from 8 EU acts (CELEX 32024R1689, 32016R0679, 32023R2854, 32022R2065, 32022L2555, 32019L0882, 32023R1781, 32019L1024), verbatim from the CS, SK and EN Official Journal editions. Each carries its CELEX number, recital number and EUR-Lex link. The attribution and Commission Decision 2011/833/EU are recorded in data/verbal/passages.json.
verbal.items: 69 statements (27 true, 21 false, 21 cannot say), each in all three languages with one key and a reason. A sitting takes 4 statements from each of 5 random passages.
checks: CI: every item's passage id exists.
CI: every quote in a reason matches its passage verbatim, in each language (this caught 10 slips while the items were being written).
CI: the format is 20/35/10, and a sitting has 20 distinct items with each passage's statements kept together.
Blind self-check: three fresh subagents, one per language, got only the passages and the statements. All 210 answers matched the key.
gdpr43-2 was dropped anyway because 'cannot say' was arguable.
ai63-4 was reworded from 'must' to 'should' and re-checked blind: 3 of 3 agreed.
Independent code review: nothing blocking. Its two non-blocking findings were fixed before merge: a reload-once if the lazy chunk has gone after a deploy, and scroll to top on Next.

verification.detail: Verified as they stood: 1052, 1072. Corrected, then verified: 1066, 1080, 2056, 2062, 2073, 2078. Unverifiable: 7 are judgments no text decides (1067, 1074, 1079, 2070, 2080, 2081, 2086); 4 rest on sources we may not pin (1002, 2043 OECD; 1073 IIA; 1077 Reg. 1049/2001 release); 1 is a negative claim (2082). Reasons: data/verification/2026-10-29.json.
checks: CI quote check passes against the 41 pinned texts. The citation floor is raised to 72 governance and 67 policy.
A blind reviewer given only the 8 verified questions and their quotes agreed on all 8.
Independent data review found nothing blocking. Its one correctness note was fixed before merge: 2073 option (a) and the explanation now cover only 2024, the period the pinned report covers.

signals_fixed: key_action verbal_start (Practice tab) and verbal_finish {lang, score, total}, the same shape as numerical_* and abstract_*. No new event names.
The verbal screen is lazy-loaded, which keeps 35 KB gzip of passages off first load for everyone who never opens it.

decisions.question: Verbal item form: true/false/cannot-say statements, or EPSO's current '4 statements, which one is correct?' per passage?
options: true / false / cannot say per statement (as briefed)
decisions.why: This is the form the brief specified, and it is checkable item by item. Moving to the 4-option form means regrouping the existing statements, with no new passages needed.

decisions.question: Verbal passages: recitals of EU acts, or articles?
decisions.why: Recitals are reasoned prose, closest to EPSO-style passages, and the test asks only what the text says, so later amendments don't matter.

decisions.question: Where does verbal sit on the Practice tab?
options: above numerical and abstract (the notice's order)
decisions.why: It follows Table 3's order and is reversible by moving one block.

decisions.question: Accept a JRC technical report and a DG Competition staff brief as sources for verification?
decisions.default_taken: accept, for the standards and competition questions only
decisions.why: No legal act names the ISO/IEC standards or the Commission's competition stance on GenAI partnerships. These are the official EU texts that do.

decisions.question: Unverifiable questions: keep, rewrite into checkable ones, or retire?
options: keep, labelled as not verified (as now)
decisions.why: The app already shows them as unverified, and retiring them would change the exam's category balance. Pavol's call.
